results.title: 'Sacré sel': France's love of salt
results.content: We take a look at a salt scandal that is rocking the UK, after Maldon sea salt was found to come, in part, from rock salt imported from Germany. We also discuss France's relationship to salt (le sel) and the different kinds in France, from fleur de sel to sel gris. Finally, we look at French history and expressions about salt.

results.title: Le Pen's top ally Bardella faces fresh allegations of anti-semitic comments
results.content: French investigative outlet Mediapart on Thursday published extracts from private conversations in which far-right leader Jordan Bardella allegedly made anti-semitic remarks as a teenager, prompting fresh accusations that he has denied.

results.title: 'We are not fighting culture, we fight to end FGM: It's a human rights violation of women and girls'
results.content: “We fight to end FGM because it is a human rights violation of women and girls. We are not fighting culture.” Caroline Lagat, Legal Advisor at Equality Now’s Africa office in Nairobi, discusses the challenges of ending female genital mutilation (FGM) and child marriage. She points to insufficient funding, conflicting marriage laws and growing community resistance to campaigns against FGM. While acknowledging some progress, Lagat calls on the government to be "the face of the campaign to end FGM and child marriage.”

results.title: Injury-hit PSG drop first points of Champions League campaign against Roma
results.content: After kicking off their Champions League title defence with four consecutive wins, Luis Enrique's men were held to a draw at home by the Italian side Roma. Real Madrid are now two points clear at the top of the standings.

results.title: Huge explosion at oil depot in Bangkok sends fireball into sky
results.content: An explosion at an oil depot in Bangkok sent a large fireball and thick black smoke into the sky, journalists said Thursday, as local authorities urged people nearby to evacuate.

results.title: Aid cuts to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further curb women's access to healthcare, education and food
results.content: Having lived and worked in Afghanistan for seven years, photojournalist Élise Blanchard offers an intimate account of what daily life is like for Afghan women today. Joining Genie Godula on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, she explains how restrictions vary across the country, depending on where women live, their families and the local enforcement of Taliban decrees. She stresses the need to maintain access to healthcare, primary education and food, pointing to severe cuts in humanitarian assistance by the US and EU.

results.title: 'Unacceptable': China, EU among major economies against new US tariffs
results.content: China, the European Union and other major trading partners on Thursday criticised new US tariffs of up to 20 percent proposed by US President Donald Trump after a probe into alleged global overcapacity, raising the prospect of fresh trade tensions with allies and rivals alike.

results.title: EU leaders face showdown over Ukraine funding as divisions deepen
results.content: European Union leaders on Thursday are set to tackle deep divisions as they meet in Brussels to discuss the bloc's long-term budget in Brussels, which includes a proposed €45 billion loan to keep Ukraine funded through 2027.

results.title: Iraqi court sentences 8 French nationals to life in prison for IS group membership
results.content: An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life in prison and two others to 15 years on Thursday for joining the Islamic State group, as Baghdad steps up prosecutions of thousands of alleged jihadists transferred from Syria.

results.title: 'It’s really outrageous': Women face violence in the streets and 'what we see online is even worse'
results.content: On International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, FRANCE 24's François Picard is pleased to welcome back Choralyne Dumésnil, an attorney practising in Paris and California, to discuss misogyny, sexual violence, cyberbullying and the challenges victims face in seeking justice. "There's always that stigma when you lodge a complaint. You get questioned, you get cross-examined," notes François Picard. Despite efforts to raise awareness, Dumésnil sees little significant change in society.

results.title: Live: EU leaders meet in Brussels amid division over Ukraine funding
results.content: EU leaders are set to clash in Brussels on Thursday over a proposed €45 billion loan to fund Ukraine in 2027, with Germany pressing members to contribute and others seeking exemption. A day earlier, US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to escalate its war with Ukraine after talks in Florida. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

results.title: US authorises SpaceX to launch up to one million satellites for orbital data centres
results.content: The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX's plan to deploy up to one million satellites to build data centres in orbit, giving Elon Musk's company a major foothold in the industry. The authorisation runs through 2040, as tech firms race to move computing infrastructure into space despite significant technical hurdles.

results.title: At least 31 killed in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns on busy highway
results.content: At least 31 people were killed and 15 injured when a fuel truck overturned and burst into flames on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, engulfing nearby vehicles, Egyptian authorities said.

results.title: Powerful US storm forces historic postponement of New York's Thanksgiving Day Parade
results.content: A powerful storm forecast to bring fierce winds and heavy rain to the northeastern United States has forced the unprecedented postponement of the city's 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade, with the event rescheduled for Saturday. Officials warned that Thursday's conditions could bring down tree limbs and power lines, while posing a safety risk to the parade's giant balloons and the crowds below.

results.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
results.content: Andy Taylor, whose guitar riffs helped shape Duran Duran's distinctive sound and propel the British band to global fame in the 1980s, has died aged 65 after a long battle with prostate cancer, the band and his family said Wednesday.

results.title: PSG's perfect Champions League record ends as Roma snatch 2-2 draw with late penalty
results.content: Donyell Malen's 78th-minute penalty earned Roma a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday, ending the defending champions' perfect record in this season's Champions League. The result also halted PSG's 12-game winning streak in all competitions, leaving Real Madrid as the only team with a 100% record after five league-phase matches.

results.title: Le Pen party leaks: prefect dismissed, Paris deputy prosecutor placed under investigation
results.content: Two senior figures in France have been caught up in an investigation into suspected leaks to the far-right party of Marine Le Pen, the National Rally. The prefect of the Loiret, Hugues Moutouh, a former top official at the Interior Ministry, has been removed from his post after being suspected of passing on confidential information about investigations. And a deputy prosecutor in Paris, who was found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now under administrative inquiry. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight reports.

results.title: Israeli lawmakers advance October 7 inquiry opposed by Netanyahu
results.content: Israel's new parliament on Wednesday took a first step to set up a state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to Hamas's unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack, a move long opposed by caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

results.title: New US tariffs: 'Trump lashing out really indiscriminately', expert says
results.content: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Dean Baker, Senior Economist at the Centre for Economic and Policy Research, says that "there has to be some mechanism for better coordinating China's involvement in the world trade system and ideally the US, the EU, Canada would have a common front, some clear ground rules that we could agree to, that China could agree to, to be mutually beneficial. It's not a step in that direction, we have President Trump lashing out really indiscriminately. It's very hard to see his approach being very productive".

results.title: Cape Town court shuts down Ramaphosa's Farmgate scandal
results.content: In tonight's edition: South Africa's president sidesteps an impeachment bid by the opposition. Also, we hear from some of the Malagasy women fighting for an overhaul of reproductive rights in their country. And in eastern DR Congo, the CRP rebel group halts its advance after coming within dozens of kilometres of the northeastern city of Bunia.

results.title: Did GTA 6 really recreate Charlie Kirk's assassination?
results.content: Just days after its release, Grand Theft Auto 6 has become a vehicle for political misinformation. Viral footage falsely claims the game features a mission recreating Charlie Kirk’s assassination, while pro-Russian accounts are sharing fake screenshots containing anti-Ukrainian messages. Meanwhile, Russia’s own Defence Ministry has exploited the game's popularity to promote military recruitment. Vedika Bahl explains how GTA 6 is being used to push real political agendas in Truth or Fake.

results.title: Campaign rules for influencers? French regulator targets content creators
results.content: Ever since 1965, when the French first got to cast a ballot by universal suffrage for their president, they've valued campaign rules that guarantee "equal time" for candidates. But what does equal time mean when you're closing in on 2027? Last week came a bombshell announcement ahead of next spring’s presidential elections: major online content creators will have to respect the same balanced airtime rules as traditional TV and radio broadcasters during the campaign period.

results.title: EU says 'strongly' rejects premise of new US tariffs
results.content: The EU said Wednesday that it rejected the premise of new tariffs on its exports proposed by the United States and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year. The US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.
